definition: Shrutlekhan-Rajbhasha is a Hindi language speech recognition software application developed by C-DAC in collaboration with IBM .
details: It takes Hindi sound as input and converts to Devanagari text as output. One drawback of this software is that if mixed English–Hindi dictation is given, it can recognize Hindi words but can not recognize English words. Another variant of this software is Vachantar-Rajbhasha, which takes English sound as input, converts it to English text and then translates it to Hindi using MANTRA-Rajbhasha translation engine.

explainer.lead: Shrutlekhan-Rajbhasha is a Hindi speech recognition application that converts spoken Hindi into Devanagari text. It matters because it provides a language-specific dictation tool for Hindi rather than relying on English-centric systems.

tiers.eli5: You speak Hindi into a microphone and the computer types it out in Hindi script. But if you mix in English words, it only catches the Hindi ones.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers deploy it for Hindi dictation where output must be in Devanagari script, and must route English terms elsewhere since it cannot recognize English words in mixed dictation. A pitfall is assuming it handles code-switched Hindi–English speech.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined operationally as a speech-to-text system mapping Hindi audio input to Devanagari text output; the stated limit is failure on English words within mixed English–Hindi dictation.

explainer.example: A user dictates a Hindi sentence containing an English product name; the software transcribes the Hindi words but drops the English one.
